when.text: Small bug with a cheap local check

approach.text: Reproduce first, then make the smallest fix

gates.text: Fail for the right reason before fixing

output.text: Named failing-before and passing-after evidence
output.detail: Report the executable check, its original failure, and the validation after the fix.

watch-out.text: Skip impractical tests; explain the alternative proof
watch-out.detail: Avoid building expensive infrastructure for a small fix and report the closest useful executable verification instead.

when.text: Features or bugs built test-first

approach.text: One public behavior per red-green cycle

gates.text: User confirms test boundaries before any test
gates.detail: List each proposed seam with what it catches and misses, then obtain user confirmation.

output.text: Tests that survive internal refactoring
output.detail: Observe behavior through public interfaces with expected values from an independent source of truth.

watch-out.text: Refactoring belongs in review, outside the loop
watch-out.detail: The implementation loop excludes refactoring and hands that work to the review stage.

when.text: New logic, bug fixes, or changed behavior

approach.text: Red, green, then refactor with tests running

gates.text: Focused test first; full suite before completion
gates.detail: Discover the repository's actual test commands rather than assuming a particular language or runner.

output.text: Regression test plus verified behavior

watch-out.text: Avoid internal-call assertions and excessive mocking
watch-out.detail: Prefer observable outcomes and real implementations unless controlled doubles are necessary.

when.text: Behavior changes and acceptance-criterion verification

approach.text: Red-green-refactor plus tests through real entry points
approach.detail: End-to-end scenarios exercise the HTTP API, CLI, UI, or queue that actual users or services use.

gates.text: Test every acceptance criterion and milestone outcome
gates.detail: Rule T2 requires coverage of each criterion and outcome without weakening or skipping tests to pass.

output.text: Verification commands and results in the report
output.detail: Record runnable verification in milestone documentation and report the command and result after executing it.

watch-out.text: Performance tests deferred; record that on the ticket

gates.text: Distinguish legitimate states from impossible ones

output.text: Root-cause fix across matching instances
output.detail: Search for the same fault pattern elsewhere and fix those occurrences rather than only the reported instance.

watch-out.text: Retries and guards can conceal the fault
watch-out.detail: Do not use swallowed errors, discarded state, or clamping as substitutes for understanding the cause.

output.text: Regression proof and a documented winning hypothesis
output.detail: Verify the original scenario after fixing and state the confirmed cause in the commit or pull request.

output.text: Minimal reproduction and recurrence-catching regression test
output.detail: Reduce the failure to its essential inputs and add a test that fails without the fix.

watch-out.detail: Investigate timing, environment, and state differences, then monitor genuinely non-reproducible cases rather than claiming certainty.

when.text: Measured slowness, regressions, or database tuning
when.detail: The workflow explicitly includes profiling database queries and indexes before tuning.

approach.text: Same baseline conditions; one change at a time
approach.detail: Compare measurements with the same command and budget so effects can be attributed to the change.

gates.text: Revert neutral, slower, or correctness-breaking changes
gates.detail: Keep an optimization only when it beats the threshold beyond noise and tests remain green.

output.text: Before-and-after numbers plus a ledger of attempts
output.detail: Record retained and reverted experiments so later work does not repeat failed ideas without context.

watch-out.text: A gain within measurement noise is not a win
watch-out.detail: Repeat measurements and compare the delta with run-to-run variation before claiming improvement.

scenarios.label: Audit a speedup claim
scenarios.reason: Error counts, actual work, tuning, and repeatability directly test measurement validity.

scenarios.label: Find application bottlenecks
scenarios.reason: Both workflows start with evidence and profile the affected experience.

scenarios.label: Track optimization experiments
scenarios.reason: The attempt ledger and explicit neutral-result reverts fit iterative performance work.

scenarios.label: Overall
scenarios.reason: Different constraints, different fits; no measured overall winner.

when.text: Existing discussion is ready to become a spec
when.detail: Synthesize the conversation and repository understanding rather than restarting requirements discovery.

approach.text: Capture stories, decisions, tests, and exclusions
approach.detail: Use domain glossary terms and relevant architectural decisions while documenting the intended feature.

human-input.text: Confirm testing boundaries, not another intent interview
human-input.detail: Propose the highest practical existing seams and check that they match the user's expectations.

output.text: Spec published to the configured issue tracker
output.detail: Publish the specification with the ready-for-agent triage label after capturing the agreed content.

watch-out.text: Avoid file paths and incidental code snippets
watch-out.detail: Allow only decision-rich prototype snippets when code expresses a settled choice better than prose.

when.text: New feature or significant change lacks a spec
when.detail: Write requirements before implementation when the work is substantial or ambiguous.

approach.text: Specify, plan, task, implement; map bundled capabilities
approach.detail: For requests containing independently testable capabilities, approve a dependency map before writing per-module specifications.

human-input.text: Human reviews every phase before advancing
human-input.detail: Validate the current artifact with the human before proceeding to the next stage.

output.text: Structured spec with commands, boundaries, and success criteria
output.detail: Capture objective, executable commands, structure, style, testing strategy, and always/ask/never boundaries.

watch-out.text: Surface assumptions before writing specification content
watch-out.detail: Do not silently fill missing requirements with guesses that later become implementation commitments.

when.text: Feature ticket needs product requirements or revised scope
when.detail: Write or update a phased PRD before design when the feature lacks a current product contract.

approach.text: Define MVP, later phases, stories, and success target
approach.detail: Specify the first usable outcome and explicitly defer later work to prevent scope creep.

human-input.text: User resolves blocking questions and reviews PRD
human-input.detail: A PRD counts only after user review, and questions affecting implementation are surfaced rather than guessed.

output.text: Docs-based PRD linked from Linear project and stories
output.detail: Publish the product document in docs with named affected services, testable criteria, and product and business metrics.

watch-out.text: Product requirements say what, not technical design
watch-out.detail: Leave engineering architecture to downstream design rather than embedding implementation decisions in the PRD.

scenarios.label: Synthesize settled discussion
scenarios.reason: Conversation synthesis avoids repeating an interview while confirming test seams.

scenarios.label: Gated engineering specification
scenarios.reason: Explicit phase reviews and capability mapping fit specification-led implementation.

scenarios.label: Product to engineering handoff
scenarios.reason: Phased PRDs link user outcomes, success metrics, services, and Linear stories.

scenarios.label: Overall
scenarios.reason: Different constraints, different fits; no measured overall winner.

when.text: Shipping production behavior or closing telemetry gaps
when.detail: Instrument alongside features and revisit observability when incidents reveal missing diagnostic evidence.

approach.text: Start with two to four on-call questions
approach.detail: Every emitted signal should answer a concrete operational question rather than merely increase logging volume.

signals.text: Structured logs, bounded metrics, and distributed traces
signals.detail: Choose logs for individual events, metrics for aggregate behavior, and OpenTelemetry traces for cross-service timing.

output.text: Correlated evidence of what happened and where
output.detail: Propagate request identifiers and entry-point attribution across boundaries so individual runs can be reconstructed.

watch-out.text: Unbounded labels and secret-bearing logs create risk
watch-out.detail: Use fixed label sets and allowlisted fields rather than raw URLs, user identifiers, or complete request bodies.

when.text: Each shipped task and instrumentation review
when.detail: New endpoints, jobs, and external calls emit technical metrics alongside the product metrics named in the PRD.

approach.text: Low-noise logs; PM owns product metric choices
approach.detail: Engineers select technical metrics while product and business metrics come from the product manager.

signals.text: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki; cross-service traces deferred
signals.detail: The named operational stack handles metrics, dashboards, and logs, while rule O7 defers traces and runbooks.

output.text: Tested metric emission now; dashboards at planned milestones
output.detail: Emission is always required, but dashboards and alerts are provisioned at the milestone specified by the plan.

watch-out.text: No per-iteration logs or duplicated metric noise
watch-out.detail: Restrict logs to boundaries, state transitions, and errors unless a recorded operational requirement justifies more.

scenarios.label: Distributed request tracing
scenarios.reason: OpenTelemetry tracing is part of the instrumentation workflow rather than deferred.

scenarios.label: Milestoned operations stack
scenarios.reason: Named tooling and staged dashboards fit the prescribed operational conventions.

scenarios.label: Production signal hygiene
scenarios.reason: Both start with operational questions and constrain labels and sensitive fields.

scenarios.label: Overall
scenarios.reason: Different constraints, different fits; no measured overall winner.
